clinicalPearls: Caused by UGT1A1 mutations that leave reduced but detectable UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 1A1 activity, giving partial conjugation capacity.
Unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia is less severe than in type 1, and kernicterus is uncommon though still possible during physiological stress.
The defining feature is a substantial fall in serum bilirubin after phenobarbital, reflecting inducible residual enzyme, which is the key distinction from type 1.
Bile contains bilirubin, predominantly as the monoglucuronide, unlike the near-absent pigment of type 1.
It sits on a severity continuum between Gilbert syndrome and type 1 and is usually inherited in an autosomal recessive manner.
Many patients live normally with a good prognosis, and treatment is needed mainly to lower bilirubin during illness, fasting, pregnancy or the neonatal period.
Phenobarbital is both diagnostic and therapeutic, while phototherapy is reserved for higher bilirubin levels or crises.
reference.pathophysiology: Crigler-Najjar syndrome type 2, also called Arias syndrome, is caused by UGT1A1 mutations that markedly reduce but do not eliminate hepatic uridine diphosphate glucuronosyltransferase 1A1 activity. Because some residual conjugating capacity persists, unconjugated bilirubin accumulates to intermediate levels, higher than in Gilbert syndrome but well below those of type 1, and the bile still contains conjugated bilirubin, predominantly as the monoglucuronide. The retained, inducible enzyme explains the hallmark biochemical response to enzyme-inducing agents such as phenobarbital, which upregulates residual UGT1A1 and lowers serum bilirubin substantially. The lower and more controllable bilirubin burden means that the lipid-soluble unconjugated pigment less often reaches neurotoxic concentrations, so kernicterus is uncommon, although it can still occur when bilirubin is driven up by intercurrent illness, prolonged fasting, dehydration or other stressors.
additionalDifferentials: Physiological and breast-milk jaundice in the neonate
Resorption of a large haematoma or extravasated blood
additionalInvestigations: Fractionated bilirubin showing predominantly unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia at intermediate levels
Phenobarbital response test, with a marked reduction supporting type 2
Haemolysis screen to exclude increased bilirubin production
Bile pigment analysis showing monoglucuronide predominance
Confirmation of otherwise normal liver function and structure
redFlags: Rising bilirubin toward neurotoxic levels during severe intercurrent illness, fasting or dehydration
Any neonatal presentation, when the immature blood-brain barrier increases kernicterus risk
Development of neurological signs suggesting bilirubin encephalopathy
Appearance of a conjugated fraction, indicating an alternative or additional diagnosis
reference.prognosis: Type 2 generally carries a good prognosis with near-normal life expectancy and a low risk of kernicterus, particularly when bilirubin is controlled during periods of physiological stress. Responsiveness to enzyme induction makes long-term management straightforward for most patients.
pitfalls: Failing to recognise that kernicterus, though rare, can still occur during stress, fasting or in the neonatal period
Not performing a phenobarbital challenge, thereby blurring the distinction from type 1 and Gilbert syndrome
Attributing an emerging conjugated fraction to the syndrome rather than seeking another cause
Assuming all congenital unconjugated jaundice is benign Gilbert syndrome
references: Inborn errors of metabolism reference texts
management: Use enzyme-inducing therapy with phenobarbital as the mainstay, exploiting the inducible residual UGT1A1 activity to substantially lower serum bilirubin
Intensify treatment during periods of physiological stress such as intercurrent illness, fasting, pregnancy and the neonatal period, when bilirubin can rise dangerously
Add phototherapy for occasional severe hyperbilirubinaemia or acute rises
Avoid precipitants including dehydration, prolonged fasting and bilirubin-displacing drugs
Monitor serum bilirubin, with heightened neurological vigilance during physiological stress given the small residual kernicterus risk
Provide genetic counselling for this autosomal recessive UGT1A1 disorder with testing of at-risk relatives
